page.layout: One printed page, single text column, no margin notes. Running head at top, page number at top right. Catchword "mihi" at the lower right of the column.

main_text.p: Abunde est, quo damna Reipublicæ sine Ecclesiæ ruinâ resarciantur. Illius quidem libenter Restaurator audiam, haud tamen eâ conditione, ut sub obtentu publici æris liberandi, hujus merito dicar Oppressor. Satis erat quæ contraxit causa improba, hoc vero pacto dissolvere, multo foret deterius. Deus faxit, ut nec Ego hec Mei funus unquam huic culpæ affines.

Ad te Domine preces meas dirigo, enixe obtestans ut hanc subditis meis ignoscas temeritatem jurandi, & acriorem in illis postea sensum effi-cias, quo illa justa, moralia, nullatenus remit-tenda vincula à Verbo Tuo & Regni Legibus conscientiis eorum imposita, accuratius in posterùm observent, à quibus multi Pietatis[?], aut Reformationis respectus satis erunt illos obsolvendo, nedum in Partem adversam transfire permittent.
Fac ut serò tandem cogitent, nil violentum & injurium cum Religione constare.
Tu nullius Sacrilegium approbas, qui sic Zelum suum offendit in detestando Idola.
Tu per Regum Sapientissimum docuisti, laqueum esse homini Sanctum devorare, ac postea ad vota converti.
Custodi Famulum Tuum usque, ne consentiat in perjuras & sacrilegas rapinas, ne stigma

page.notes: Printed ornament marks (a small bullet before "Custodi" and a small mark before "Fac ut" and "Ad te") are printer's signs, not text, and are left out. The large initial "A" of "Ad" is set as a decorative letter and is read as "Ad". "Pietatis" is read as "Pictatis" in the scan and is marked [?]. The gap above "Ad te" and the gap above "Fac ut" are spacing only. The word "hec" is printed as shown. The running head is in Greek and Latin characters as printed; the final letter of the Greek word is read as Η.
